title: Probing Homogeneity in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Steps vs. Final Answers

original_idea.title: Probing Homogeneity in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Steps vs. Final Answers
original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether inter-model homogeneity is primarily a surface-level phenomenon (shared phrasing) or reflects deeper structural similarity in reasoning chains.
original_idea.direction: Extract and compare chain-of-thought reasoning traces from multiple models on the same set of dilemma-style prompts, measuring structural similarity of reasoning steps separately from final answer similarity.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Homogeneous reasoning structures imply shared blind spots in how models reach conclusions, not just in what they say -- a deeper and more dangerous form of monoculture.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind focuses on output-level homogeneity; reasoning-level analysis would be a meaningful extension. Reasoning models (o3, DeepSeek-R1) make chain-of-thought explicit.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: homogeneous reasoning implies shared blind spots in how models reach conclusions, a deeper and more dangerous form of monoculture than surface-level similarity.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: extracting and structurally comparing CoT traces requires developing a comparison methodology, which involves moderate analytical sophistication.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: structural comparison of reasoning traces vs. final answers on a fixed set of dilemma prompts across multiple models.

novelty.reasoning: Research on CoT structural analysis exists: 'Verifying Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Its Computational Graph' (2025) analyzes structural fingerprints of correct vs. incorrect reasoning. 'Diagnosing Pathological Chain-of-Thought in Reasoning Models' (2025) examines CoT failures. However, no published work specifically compares inter-model homogeneity at the reasoning-step level vs. the final-answer level. The Artificial Hivemind focuses on output-level similarity only. The structural reasoning homogeneity angle is mostly novel.
